items.grounds: Confirmed by re-derivation. The sentence's antecedent, the quoted summons run הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier), stands at 1 verse book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 1 verse), and its two-word head likewise (sweep: 1 verse). The figure 5 belongs to the single token הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier): its skeleton stands at 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses - oshb:Isa.1.10, oshb:Isa.8.9, oshb:Isa.28.23, oshb:Isa.51.4, oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4), an object the sentence never names. At the fifth site the bytes read לֹ֣א הֶאֱזִ֑ינוּ (oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, byte tier): the verb is vocalized segol + hataf-segol against the imperative's patah + hataf-patah - a perfect, mid-verse - so the substring blend crosses speech classes, and only the oshb:Isa.28.23 site is verse-initial, against the row's 'spread across openings' framing. One splice nit against the finding, without effect on its substance: its site quote carries only the negator; the perfect is the following token. A count-object mismatch on a non-load-bearing typing concession: medium as filed.

Confirmed. The shipped rear edge argues the next onset from a transliteration over web:Isa.29.1, and boundary_evidence_refs carries no oshb:Isa.29.1 (re-checked against the shipped row). The onset claim itself is byte-true: ה֚וֹי אֲרִיאֵ֣ל אֲרִיאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.29.1, byte tier) opens the verse, a ruled woe-onset of the 28-33 hoy series, so nothing is byte-false and the boundary stands. But pointed splices with tier labels are mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim, and this rear-edge warrant ships rendering-only: a defective warrant, not a mere mechanical slip. The close is co-warranted by the quoted closing-verse content at web:Isa.28.29 and its disclosed single-witness setumah, so the defect is not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

Confirmed. Collated as quoted, מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ תִּפָּקֵ֔ד (oshb:Isa.29.6, byte tier) reaches tier none against the oshb:Isa.28.29 window - its fourth word has no counterpart there - so the two quoted runs meet at no tier. What recurs is the three-word phrase: מֵעִ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת (oshb:Isa.28.29, byte tier) collates at accent_stripped tier inside oshb:Isa.29.6 and oshb:Isa.8.18, standing at 1 verse at byte tier and exactly 3 verses at accent_stripped tier (sweep: 3 verses - oshb:Isa.8.18, oshb:Isa.28.29, oshb:Isa.29.6). The row's tier label and 3-verse digit are right; its quoted comparison is false at the quoted extent. The device is a disclosed cross-seam signal, not the seam's carrier - the front seam rides the hoy onset - so a defective recurrence claim, not a load-bearing falsehood: medium as filed.

Confirmed. The shipped rear edge argues the fresh onset from the rendering over web:Isa.29.9, with no oshb:Isa.29.9 in boundary_evidence_refs (re-checked). The claim is byte-true: הִתְמַהְמְה֣וּ וּתְמָ֔הוּ הִשְׁתַּֽעַשְׁע֖וּ וָשֹׁ֑עוּ (oshb:Isa.29.9, byte tier) opens the verse. The finding's contrast digits also re-derive exactly: the name-chain skeleton stands at 3 verses book-wide with 5 token occurrences (sweep: 3 verses - oshb:Isa.29.1, oshb:Isa.29.2, oshb:Isa.29.7), and כָּל הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל (oshb:Isa.29.7, byte tier) holds at byte tier across exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses - oshb:Isa.29.7, oshb:Isa.29.8). Under the mandatory pointed-splice discipline for boundary-relevant Hebrew claims the rendering-only rear edge is a defective warrant; the edge itself is correct and co-warranted by the quoted close at web:Isa.29.8 with its disclosed single-witness setumah: medium as filed.

Confirmed. As quoted the bridge fails: הַיֹּצֵ֖ר יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב (oshb:Isa.29.16, byte tier) reaches tier none against the oshb:Isa.29.17 window, and וְהַכַּרְמֶ֖ל לַיַּ֥עַר יֵחָשֵֽׁב (oshb:Isa.29.17, byte tier) reaches tier none against oshb:Isa.29.16 - the claimed skeleton-tier sharing does not hold at the quoted extents. The shared verb alone holds, and only at skeleton tier: יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב (oshb:Isa.29.16, byte tier) collates at skeleton tier in oshb:Isa.29.17, and יֵחָשֵֽׁב (oshb:Isa.29.17, byte tier) at skeleton tier in oshb:Isa.29.16; both forms carry U+05BD at different positions and accent-stripping retains U+05BD, so skeleton is the lowest agreeing tier - the row's tier choice is right for the verb, wrong for its quoted runs. The bridge also ships without a distribution digit; re-swept, the verb's skeleton stands at 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses - oshb:Isa.10.7, oshb:Isa.13.17, oshb:Isa.29.16, oshb:Isa.29.17, oshb:Isa.32.15). The row's stated internal-cohesion evidence is byte-true in substance yet defectively quoted and un-digited: medium as filed, not high.

Confirmed. Re-swept, the contiguous skeleton substring ספר stands at exactly 20 verses book-wide (sweep: 20 verses) and exactly 4 in Isa.28-31 (sweep: 4 verses - oshb:Isa.29.11, oshb:Isa.29.12, oshb:Isa.29.18, oshb:Isa.30.8), every in-window matching token the scroll noun, so the in-window digit is sound. The 20 blends count objects: it includes the number noun מִסְפָּ֣ר (oshb:Isa.10.19, byte tier; also oshb:Isa.21.17, oshb:Isa.40.26), the scribe noun סֹפֵר֙ (oshb:Isa.33.18, byte tier; also oshb:Isa.36.3), the recount-verb family סְפַרְתֶּ֑ם (oshb:Isa.22.10, byte tier; also oshb:Isa.43.21, oshb:Isa.43.26, oshb:Isa.52.15 - two sites beyond the finding's floor, its 'at minimum' hedge holding), and the place name סְפַרְוָ֑יִם (oshb:Isa.36.19, byte tier; also oshb:Isa.37.13): 11 of the 20 verses carry no scroll-noun token. The finding's K/Q check also re-derives: 1 K/Q note at oshb:Isa.29.11 (single-witness), and the quoted הַסֵּ֣פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.11, byte tier) stands before the staged doubled pair הספר סֵ֛פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.11, byte tier, first token the unpointed ketiv) later in the verse. A digit attributed to the named noun while counting a blended substring family is a defective count claim on a disclosure device, not a boundary carrier: medium as filed.

Confirmed. The shipped rear edge argues the koh-amar address from the rendering over web:Isa.29.22 - no oshb:Isa.29.22 in boundary_evidence_refs, and the closing sentence names no frame owner (re-checked). The claim is byte-true and verse-initial: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.29.22, byte tier), the tetragrammaton standing as speaker - a divine frame, and oshb:Isa.29.22 is not among the four royal-messenger koh-amar sites (oshb:Isa.36.4, oshb:Isa.36.14, oshb:Isa.36.16, oshb:Isa.37.3), the ruled role split that requires every koh-amar claim to name whose frame it engages. Rendering-only support plus the unnamed frame owner make a defective rear-edge warrant under the mandatory pointed-splice discipline; the edge itself is correct and co-warranted by the quoted close at web:Isa.29.21 with its disclosed single-witness setumah: medium as filed.
